cells.tense: You are still here, and the hoping has outlasted everything that tried to end it.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Take the hardest thing you're carrying and do the next real step on it, whatever the step actually is, before anything else today.
cells.core:
You keep hoping past the point other people quit, and it isn't naivety; you've been through enough that the hope got tested and stayed. The same steadiness is what lets you sit beside people without needing them to hurry up and be fine. You can feel with someone and not be swept off your feet by it. When that's working, the other person gets room to move at their own speed.

The risk right now is that your endurance runs quietly, pointed at the work and not at the people in it. So take the heaviest thing you carry and move on it once. Just the next piece of it. Then look up and notice who has been standing nearby, steady in the same way you are.
cells.sheetLine: The hope survived everything, and so did your aim.
cells.verb: keep going after everything, because you still hope for it
cells.place: beside the people you keep turning toward, close enough to feel with them

cells.tense: You will keep going no matter what, and you are already bracing for what that keeping will cost.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: On a coming decision, write the best and worst outcome side by side, close the page, and leave both alone until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You are going to keep going, that much is settled. The bracing comes from having already run the whole thing forward in your head — every way it can fail, every part of you it will take — so the shape of how this goes is being written before it happens. It doesn't get softer with rehearsal. It gets louder.

Your mind already knows how to hold a thing before saying it. Let that happen with the near future too. When a prediction swirls at you, give it a page and a night to prove itself, then read what you actually wrote. A lot of what got announced last week didn't arrive. Both versions can sit there, unanswered, until one of them earns it.
cells.sheetLine: You run the future early, then live as if it already happened.
cells.verb: keep going after everything, because you still hope for it
cells.place: beside the people you keep turning toward, close enough to feel with them

cells.tense: You held the line for so long that holding on became the only thing you were doing.
cells.ask: Choose something still growing — a plant, a person, a piece of work — and give it only what it needs this week, then leave it be.
cells.core:
You kept going through something that took a lot, and you're still keeping going now that it's done. The people who come close meet the part of you that endures instead of the part of you that's here. Catching up to right now is still available to you. It happens in ordinary minutes, not in a big decision.

Care is the way back, without squeezing. Take one thing still growing and tend it for a week. Give it water, give it space, and skip the hourly check. Looking after what you care about without crushing it is already in your hands. Do that with something small, and the present gets easier to land in.
cells.sheetLine: Spend the week on what's growing, and let today catch up.
cells.verb: keep going after everything, because you still hope for it

cells.tense: You are carrying the whole load again and still calling it a string of lucky breaks.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Name one hard thing you got through that you credit to timing or luck, and say it as yours, with the disclaimer left off.
cells.core:
What you do beside people is keep going — including after they've quit, including when it's expensive. That is the same resilience that lets you sit with someone in a hard season without rushing them toward better news. You can stay close to pain and not be swallowed by it. The people near you get a companion who isn't frightened by how long something takes.

The trouble is that you book your own endurance under circumstance: it worked out, they happened to stay, the timing was right. That leaves you standing beside something you built and calling it weather. So pick one load you carried and say its name as yours. No disclaimer, no shrinking it to what anyone would have done.
cells.sheetLine: The name on the endurance is yours and unsigned.
cells.verb: keep going after everything, because you still hope for it
cells.place: beside the people you keep turning toward, close enough to feel with them

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that their persistence is currently landing as connection, or that people feel steadied by it — the seat is Compassion, but the card only says persistence keeps going, not what it does for anyone near them. A reader could reasonably say the endurance is private, or that it costs the people close to them rather than holding them. The asks survive being wrong: each one is the medicine's own act, doable even if the reading misses. The sentence that serves me is the Too Little line about a door already behind — it sounds like closure and they never told me there was a door.
